title: Osman I founds the Ottoman state
summary: Osman, leader of a small Turkish beylik on the Byzantine frontier, begins the expansion of what becomes the Ottoman Empire.

title: Closing of Venice's Great Council (Serrata)
summary: Membership of the Great Council becomes hereditary for families already sitting in it. Venice becomes a closed aristocratic republic — a constitution that lasted 500 years.

title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
summary: Mansa Musa of Mali passes through Cairo with thousands of attendants and so much gold that its price in Egypt collapses for years. Europe's maps begin to show him on his throne.

title: Mexica found Tenochtitlan
summary: The Mexica (Aztecs) found their city on an island in Lake Texcoco where, legend says, they saw an eagle on a cactus eating a snake. It grew into one of the largest cities in the world.

title: Hundred Years' War begins
summary: Edward III of England claims the French throne, starting a series of wars that last until 1453 and help forge English and French national identities.

title: Battle of Crécy
summary: English longbowmen cut down the charging French knights — a sign that the age of chivalric cavalry was ending.

title: The Black Death
summary: Plague arrives from the Black Sea on Genoese ships and kills perhaps a third to half of Europe's population; the Middle East and North Africa are devastated too. Venice loses around half its people in 1348.
significance: Venice responded with some of the first public-health measures: quarantine (from 'quaranta giorni', forty days) and plague hospitals on lagoon islands.

title: Ming dynasty founded
summary: Zhu Yuanzhang, a former beggar and monk, drives out the Mongol Yuan and founds the Ming dynasty.

title: War of Chioggia
summary: Genoa seizes Chioggia and threatens Venice itself. The Venetians blockade the Genoese in turn and force their surrender in 1380; the Peace of Turin (1381) ends a century of rivalry in Venice's favour.

title: Battle of Kosovo
summary: Ottoman and Serbian armies clash; both rulers, Sultan Murad I and Prince Lazar, are killed. Serbia soon becomes an Ottoman vassal.

title: Battle of Nicopolis
summary: A great crusading army of French, Hungarian and other knights, supported by a Venetian fleet, is destroyed by Sultan Bayezid I.

title: Timur sacks Delhi
summary: The Central Asian conqueror Timur (Tamerlane) sacks Delhi, slaughtering much of its population and leaving the Delhi Sultanate crippled.

title: Battle of Ankara
summary: Timur defeats and captures Sultan Bayezid I. The Ottoman state nearly collapses in civil war, giving Byzantium half a century more of life.

title: Zheng He's treasure voyages
summary: Admiral Zheng He leads seven huge Ming fleets — some ships may have been over 100 m long — across the Indian Ocean to India, Arabia and the Swahili coast. Then the Ming court abruptly stops the voyages.

title: Venice conquers Padua, Verona and Vicenza
summary: Turning to the mainland, Venice takes Padua, Verona and Vicenza. Its 'Terraferma' state soon reaches Brescia and Bergamo, near Milan.

title: Forbidden City completed
summary: The Yongle Emperor moves the Ming capital to Beijing and completes the vast imperial palace complex.

title: Battle of Agincourt
summary: Henry V's outnumbered English army defeats the French nobility on a muddy field.

title: Jan Hus burned at Constance
summary: The Czech reformer is executed as a heretic despite a promise of safe conduct, sparking the Hussite Wars in Bohemia.

title: Portuguese voyages along Africa begin
summary: Prince Henry 'the Navigator' sponsors voyages down the African coast; Madeira and the Azores are settled and the caravel is perfected.

title: Joan of Arc relieves Orléans
summary: A peasant girl who heard divine voices leads a French army to lift the English siege of Orléans, turning the tide of the Hundred Years' War. She was burned in 1431.

title: Pachacuti begins the Inca Empire
summary: Pachacuti defeats the Chanka and transforms the Kingdom of Cusco into Tawantinsuyu, the Inca Empire — eventually the largest state in the Americas.

title: Machu Picchu built
summary: The Inca build Machu Picchu as a royal estate for Pachacuti on a ridge high above the Urubamba valley.

title: Cosimo de' Medici takes power in Florence
summary: The banker Cosimo de' Medici returns from exile and becomes the unofficial ruler of Florence, patron of Brunelleschi, Donatello and the early Renaissance.

title: Florence Cathedral dome completed
summary: Filippo Brunelleschi completes the largest brick dome ever built, without wooden centring — a symbol of the Renaissance.

title: King Sejong creates Hangul
summary: King Sejong the Great and his scholars invent Hangul, a simple phonetic alphabet so that ordinary Koreans could read and write.

title: Gutenberg Bible printed
summary: Johannes Gutenberg prints the Bible with movable metal type. By 1500 there are printing presses in over 250 European cities — Venice becomes the printing capital of Europe.

title: Fall of Constantinople
summary: After a 53-day siege, Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II storms the walls with the help of giant cannon. The last Byzantine emperor, Constantine XI, dies fighting; Venetian and Genoese volunteers were among the defenders.
significance: The end of the Roman Empire in the east. Istanbul becomes the Ottoman capital, and Venice must now deal with a superpower on its doorstep.

title: Peace of Lodi
summary: Venice and Milan end their long wars. Together with Florence, Naples and the Papacy, they form the Italian League, giving Italy 40 years of relative balance-of-power peace.

title: Wars of the Roses
summary: The houses of York and Lancaster fight for the English throne; Henry Tudor wins at Bosworth in 1485.

title: Ōnin War begins Japan's Warring States era
summary: A succession dispute in the shogunate burns much of Kyoto and plunges Japan into a century of civil war (Sengoku).

title: Ottomans take Negroponte from Venice
summary: Mehmed II captures Venice's key Aegean base after a bloody siege, during the long First Ottoman–Venetian War (1463–1479).

title: Venice acquires Cyprus
summary: Caterina Cornaro, the Venetian-born widowed queen of Cyprus, is persuaded to cede her kingdom to the Republic.

title: Fall of Granada
summary: Ferdinand and Isabella take Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, completing the Reconquista. Months later they expel Spain's Jews.

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
summary: Sailing west for Castile in search of Asia, the Genoese navigator Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas, then Cuba and Hispaniola.
significance: The beginning of permanent contact between the hemispheres — the 'Columbian Exchange' of crops, animals and diseases that devastated Indigenous peoples and reshaped every continent.

title: Treaty of Tordesillas
summary: Spain and Portugal divide the newly found lands outside Europe along a meridian west of the Cape Verde islands — which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.

title: French invasion of Italy
summary: Charles VIII of France marches into Italy to claim Naples, shattering the Peace of Lodi and starting 60 years of Italian Wars between France and Spain.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
summary: Sailing around Africa, Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut. A Portuguese sea route to the spices of Asia now bypasses the Venetian and Mamluk middlemen.
significance: When the news arrived, Venetian diarist Girolamo Priuli called it the worst news Venice had ever received.

title: Askia Muhammad rules Songhai
summary: Askia the Great seizes power in the Songhai Empire, which has replaced Mali as the dominant power of the western Sahel; Timbuktu flourishes as a centre of learning.

title: Great Temple of Tenochtitlan rededicated
summary: Under Ahuitzotl the Aztecs rededicate the Templo Mayor with huge ceremonies. The Aztec Triple Alliance now dominates central Mexico.

title: Great Stand on the Ugra River
summary: Ivan III of Moscow faces down the Great Horde without battle, ending the 'Tatar yoke' over Russia. Moscow claims to be the 'Third Rome'.

title: Ottomans capture Otranto
summary: An Ottoman force lands in southern Italy and takes Otranto, terrifying Rome; it withdraws after Mehmed II's death the next year.
